The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has approved the promotion of 7,714 workers in the FCT, including 4,220 teachers and 3,494 other civil servants. The approval followed the conclusion of the 2025 and 2026 promotion exercises conducted by the FCT Civil Service Commission. The Chairman of the commission, Emeka Ezeh, announced the development on Tuesday in a statement shared on X by the minister’s media aide, Lere Olayinka. “The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, Nyesom Wike, has approved the promotion of 4,220 Teachers and 3,494 other civil servants following the conclusion of the 2025 and 2026 promotion exercise conducted by the FCT Civil Service Commission (CSC),” the statement read. Ezeh described the approval as part of efforts by the Wike-led FCT Administration to boost workers’ morale. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources He said the minister had directed the commission to clear inherited promotion backlogs and ensure that eligible civil servants were promoted. “You will also recall that the Minister approved that Education officers who disrupted the 2025 promotion exercise be pardoned and allowed to participate in the 2026 exercise. “The Commission subsequently invited all 2025 and 2026 eligible education officers to participate in the just concluded exercise,” he said. The commission chairman congratulated the successful candidates and urged workers to reciprocate the gesture through the diligent discharge of their duties. Ezeh also announced that the commission would hold its second pre-retirement workshop for FCTA workers scheduled to retire between January 1 and March 31, 2027. He said the workshop, scheduled for December 16, 2026, was designed to prepare the workers for life outside the public service. A total of 116 FCTA workers are expected to retire in the first quarter of 2027. In July, Wike approved the promotion of 3,592 civil servants following the conclusion of the 2025 promotion exercise conducted by the commission. The approval came after the commission conducted promotion examinations for senior officers between July 1 and 3, while junior officers sat for theirs on July 10. In October, about 5,990 education officers began their 2026 promotion examinations following Wike’s intervention, which allowed officers who could not participate in the 2025 exercise to take the test. The earlier exercise for education officers had been disrupted, preventing some eligible workers from completing their examinations.
